VBO:0200250.summary: Loyal and placid in its breed association’s ideal, the Bull Arab combines an independent outlook with a determined work ethic. Bred in Australia to find and control feral pigs, it balances speed and endurance with strength. Its moderate proportions reflect that balance between power and movement.
VBO:0200250.shortDescription: A determined Australian hunting dog, bred for speed and strength; its association values loyalty and a placid nature.

sources.title: Australian Bullarab Breeders Association — breed standard
sources.evidence: Actual complete standard read. Temperament is an association ideal: kind/loyal, balanced/placid, independent, strong determination and busy work ethic. General characteristics specify finding and controlling feral boar with speed, endurance and strength, and moderate balanced proportions. Head/ears/body/feet/full low-set tapering natural tail/short coat clauses supply independent standing morphology. No aggression, child safety, health or individual temperament guarantee is adopted.

sources.title: Australian Bullarab Breeders Association — association format
sources.evidence: Actual complete objectives and policy read. ABBA maintains a register and excludes known or suspected crosses; ANKC registration is described as a long-term goal, not existing recognition. Copyright footer 2007–2013 is not a current census; Fresh L current HTTP200 body matches retained K exactly.

sources.title: Kneipp et al., original 2021 eastern Australian dog study — actual signalment and husbandry results
sources.evidence: Actual Methods study design/owner questionnaire, Sample Population and complete Signalment/Clinical Presentation introductory results personally reread. Owner-reported Bull Arab15% separately from Bull Arab crossed with large breeds47%,2016–2019 sample. These observations corroborate living named hunting population only. Secondary ancestry/history citations and disease outcomes excluded. Remaining laboratory/results/discussion/reference bodies not freshly read or used.

VBO:0200209.summary: Affectionate and eager for company, Boxadors often want to be where their people are. Food and games of fetch are strong attractions in veterinarian Pippa Elliott’s account of these lively dogs. The Boxer–Labrador Retriever cross varies in proportions and ear carriage, without one fixed appearance.
VBO:0200209.shortDescription: A lively Boxer–Labrador Retriever cross, drawn to company, food and games of fetch.

sources.title: DogZone — Boxador, by Dr Pippa Elliott BVMS MRCVS
sources.evidence: Actual complete substantive authored body read. Direct introduction describes lively/loving dogs attracted to owner company and food; Trainability directly describes seeking owner attention and food, while direct cross-specific Exercise sentence describes fetch/Frisbee. Public copy uses those exact scopes. Entire Character section explicitly derives traits from parents and is excluded, as are parent histories, anxiety, medical/suitability, training/exercise prescriptions and guarantees. Literal Appearance describes robust athletic build, long legs/deep chest/tuck, drop ears/short coat and full straight or slightly curved tail; no always-wagging claim.
